findings.claim: The key fact 'For uniform (constant) acceleration, use $$v^2 = u^2 + 2as$$' and its worked example sit inside <div class="higher-only">.
findings.truth: The relationship is examined at both tiers, so Foundation readers lost the equation, the worked example and the only explanation of when to use it.
findings.evidence: spec P4.2 outcome 7 ('select and apply (final speed)2 - (initial speed)2 = 2 x acceleration x distance') is not bold in physics-b-21c-J259-bold.md, and P4.2.7 is not bold in the select-and-apply table in section 5h. Knowledge check 2, flashcard 4, the exam tip and takeaway 3 all test it with no tier flag.

findings.claim:
Graphs and Calculations: Exam Technique

sits outside the higher-only wrapper that follows it, so Foundation readers met the heading with nothing under it.
findings.truth: Almost all of the paragraph is both-tier: gradient of a distance-time graph, gradient of a velocity-time graph and area under the line. Only the enclosed-areas clause is Higher, so the wrapper comes off and that clause is tagged in place.
findings.evidence: spec P4.2 outcomes 8 and 9 and the P4.2 narrative ('The distance travelled can be calculated from the area under the line on a speed-time graph') are not bold; P4.2.10 ('interpret enclosed areas in velocity - time graphs') is bold.

findings.claim: Practice question 5 is typed '4 marks - Required Practical Method'.
findings.truth: OCR B has no required practicals. Practical work is organised into eight Practical Activity Groups; the trolley, ramp and light gate method is PAG3 (Motion).
findings.evidence: spec section 'Compliance with the requirements for practical work' (PAG1-PAG8) and outcomes P4.2.3b and P4.2.6b, both tagged PAG3.

findings.claim:
Conservation of Momentum: Worked Example

sits outside the higher-only wrapper that follows it.
findings.truth: Conservation of momentum is Higher only, so the heading belongs inside the wrapper. As it stood, Foundation readers met an empty heading.
findings.evidence: spec P4.3 outcome 4 ('recall and apply the equation for momentum and describe examples of the conservation of momentum in collisions') is bold.

findings.claim: 'In a perfectly elastic collision both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved, a distinction the examiner often tests.'
findings.truth: The exam claim is invented, and the elastic/inelastic distinction is not in this specification at all. The physics is kept and labelled as beyond the course rather than deleted.
findings.evidence: 'elastic collision', 'inelastic' and 'impulse' return no hits anywhere in physics-b-21c-J259.md.

findings.claim: 'The crumple zone question is one of the most frequently lost marks in this topic.'
findings.truth: An invented exam claim. The tip also carried no tier flag although the whole crumple-zone argument is Higher only.
findings.evidence: spec P4.3 outcome 5 ('select and apply Newton's second law in calculations relating force, change in momentum and time') and the P4.3 narrative 'In situations involving a change in momentum (such as a collision), the longer the duration of the impact, the smaller the average force' are both bold.

findings.claim: Takeaway 3 states 'Momentum p = mv is conserved in collisions. Crumple zones extend collision time...' with no tier prefix.
findings.truth: The whole bullet is Higher-only content and takes a 'Higher tier:' prefix (takeaways never take a wrapper).
findings.evidence: spec P4.3 outcomes 4 and 5 are bold; momentum is also bold in the equations table in section 5h.

findings.claim: Practice questions 3 (cyclist momentum, then average braking force) and 6 (lorry and car collision) carry no (HT) tag.
findings.truth: Both are pure momentum questions and are Higher only.
findings.evidence: spec P4.3 outcomes 4 and 5, both bold.

findings.claim: Flashcards 4, 5, 6 and 7 (momentum, conservation of momentum, impulse equation, crumple zone mechanism) carry no tier tag.
findings.truth: All four test Higher-only content; the tag goes at the end of the question.
findings.evidence: spec P4.3 outcomes 4 and 5 and the bold P4.3 narrative on impact duration.

findings.claim: The higher-only wrapper spans both the ratio paragraph n18 and the whole 'Worked Example: Half-Life Calculation' collapsible (n19-n22).
findings.truth: Only the net-decline ratio is Higher. Explaining half-life and reading half-life off an activity-time graph are both-tier, so Foundation readers lost the unit's only worked half-life example even though practice question 2 and knowledge check 3 test exactly that skill with no tier flag. The wrapper now closes after n18.
findings.evidence: spec P5.1 outcome 11 ('calculate the net decline, expressed as a ratio, in a radioactive emission after a given (integral) number of half-lives') is bold; outcomes 10 and 12 are not.

findings.claim: Takeaway 3 and flashcard 8 give the fraction remaining after n half-lives with no tier tag.
findings.truth: Expressing the net decline as a ratio is Higher only, so the sentence takes a Higher-tier tag and the flashcard question takes '(HT)' at the end.
findings.evidence: spec P5.1 outcome 11 is bold.

findings.claim: Nuclear fission and nuclear fusion are each wrapped in <div class="higher-only"> and both collapsible titles end '(HT)'. The wrapper sits inside the collapsible, so a Foundation reader who opens 'Nuclear Fission - Splitting the Nucleus (HT)' finds an empty box.
findings.truth: P5.3 is separate science only, which this qualification is, and none of its four outcomes is bold, so fission, the chain reaction and fusion are all assessed at both tiers. Foundation readers lost a whole topic that they are examined on.
findings.evidence: spec P5.3 'How can radioactive materials be used to provide energy? (separate science only)', outcomes 1 to 4, none bold in physics-b-21c-J259-bold.md.

findings.claim: 'Beta particles penetrate a few millimetres of aluminium.'
findings.truth: A few millimetres of aluminium stops beta particles. As written, the sentence teaches the opposite of the spec statement, and lesson 4 of this unit gets it right.
findings.evidence: spec P5.2 outcome 1 (penetration properties of alpha, beta and gamma); lesson 4 n11 'stopped by a few millimetres of aluminium'.

findings.claim: The only account of imaging inside the body is a PET scan explained through positron-electron annihilation.
findings.truth: The words positron, PET, tracer, annihilation, background radiation and dose appear nowhere in this specification. What P5.2.3 expects is a short-half-life gamma emitter whose gamma rays leave the body and are picked up by detectors outside it. That method is now stated first and the PET detail is labelled as beyond the course rather than removed. The key fact n15, knowledge check 2 and flashcards 3 and 4 are still PET-centred; they are left alone because rewriting them would ripple through narration for no mark gain once the spec method is present.
findings.evidence: spec P5.2 outcome 3 ('describe the different uses of nuclear radiations for exploration of internal organs, and for control or destruction of unwanted tissue'); grep of physics-b-21c-J259.md returns no hits for positron / PET / tracer / annihil / background radiation / dose.

findings.claim: Practice question 3 (why a long half-life makes a contaminant more dangerous) is typed '3 marks - Explain (HT)'.
findings.truth: This is both-tier content, so the (HT) tag wrongly told Foundation students to skip it.
findings.evidence: spec P5.2 outcome 5 ('explain why the hazards associated with radioactive material differ according to the radiation emitted and the half-life involved') is not bold.

findings.claim: Practice question 6 runs 9:00 am to 3:40 pm on a 110-minute half-life and the key gives 'fraction = (0.5)^(400/110) ~ 0.079' and asks for 'the fraction stated with units'.
findings.truth: Recomputation: 400 minutes / 110 = 3.636 half-lives and (0.5)^3.636 = 0.0804, not 0.079; a fraction has no units. The spec limits this calculation to a whole number of half-lives, so the time is moved to 2:30 pm (330 minutes = exactly 3 half-lives, fraction 1/8) and the key is rewritten. The question is Higher only.
findings.evidence: recomputation: 330 / 110 = 3; (1/2)^3 = 1/8 = 0.125. spec P5.1 outcome 11 says '(integral) number of half-lives' and is bold.

findings.claim: 'Answers that only list one side score half the marks.'
findings.truth: An invented mark-scheme claim. Replaced with a factual statement that a one-sided answer is incomplete.
findings.evidence: no mark-scheme claim of this kind appears in the spec; house rule on invented exam claims.

findings.claim: Description: 'Medical and industrial uses, exposure dose and radioactive waste.'
findings.truth: The lesson has no industrial uses, no dose measurement and no radioactive waste content. It covers irradiation and contamination, health risk, medical uses, background radiation, fission and fusion.
findings.evidence: read against the lesson's own content_html.

findings.claim: Flashcard 12 reads 'What fills in the blank: Cloze: _____ occurs when radioactive material gets onto or inside the body...' with the one-word answer 'Contamination.'
findings.truth: Generator boilerplate left in the stem. The stem becomes a 'Name the process' question and the answer is given in full.
findings.evidence: house flashcard rules: a one-word answer needs a 'What is / Name' question and a fuller answer.

findings.claim: Chapter mapping for this unit.
findings.truth: The unit maps to Chapter P4 (Explaining motion) for lessons 1-3 and Chapter P5 (Radioactive materials) for lessons 4-5. Radioactive materials is P5, not P6; P6 is Matter - models and explanations, which is covered by the sibling unit physics-particle-models-universe. J259 has no paper 1 / paper 2 content split: both the Breadth paper (01 Foundation / 03 Higher) and the Depth paper (02 / 04) are 90 marks, 1 hour 45 minutes, 50% each, and both assess all chapters. No lesson in this unit claims a paper split.
findings.evidence: spec section 2a (content overview and assessment overview) and the assessment approach section.

findings.claim: Assessable outcomes in the mapped chapters that this unit never teaches.
findings.truth: P4.2.4 (convert between m/s and km/h); P4.2.11 (recall the value of acceleration in free fall); P4.3.3 (scale drawings of vector diagrams, Higher); P4.3.8, P4.3.9 and P4.3.10 (forces that cause rotation, moment of a force = force x distance, levers and gears - separate science only, both tiers, and the moment equation is on the recall-and-apply list); P4.3.14 (methods of measuring human reaction times and typical results, with its own practical). None of these appears in any of the three OCR B separate physics units in the retro queue. Building the missing content is outside a fact-check.
findings.evidence: grep across separate-sciences-ocr-b physics unit raw files for 'moment of a force', 'levers and gears', 'reaction time', 'free fall', 'km/h', 'scale drawing', 'vector diagram'.

findings.claim: Lesson 3 names 'impulse' and gives impulse = F x delta t = delta p.
findings.truth: The word impulse is not spec vocabulary for J259, but the underlying relationship is: change in momentum = resultant force x time for which it acts, a Higher-tier select-and-apply equation. Left as taught; the equation itself is right.
findings.evidence: spec P4.3 outcome 5 and section 5h table (b), both bold.

findings.claim: Lesson 5 teaches background radiation, and lessons 4 and 5 both use 'dose'.
findings.truth: Neither term appears in J259. The material is correct and useful context for the IaS4 risk-benefit discussion, so it is kept without a label.
findings.evidence: grep of physics-b-21c-J259.md for 'background' and 'dose'.

findings.claim: Knowledge checks carry Higher-only content in lesson 3 (KC2 and KC5, both crumple zones argued through change in momentum).
findings.truth: No tier-tag convention exists for knowledge checks anywhere in this fleet, so nothing is edited. If a convention is agreed, these two are the items to tag.
findings.evidence: checked prior _edits.json across the retro programme: no knowledge_checks tier tags exist.

findings.claim: Lesson 4 practice question 6 uses the (1/2)^4 fraction but is left untagged.
findings.truth: It is a 6-mark extended response whose second half (why a short half-life suits a medical tracer) is both-tier. Tagging the whole question Higher would remove a both-tier task from Foundation students, which is the worse error.
findings.evidence: spec P5.1 outcome 11 (bold) versus P5.2 outcomes 3 and 5 (not bold).

summary: Five lessons, 19 findings (1 HIGH, 15 MEDIUM, 3 LOW) plus 6 notes, 32 edits. The dominant fault is the Higher-tier wrapper. Fission and fusion (P5.3, separate science only but not bold) were hidden from Foundation readers inside collapsibles titled '(HT)' that then opened empty; v2 = u2 + 2as and the unit's only worked half-life example were also wrapped although both are both-tier; and two wrapper openings sat below their headings. Pulling that content back out then needed tier tags on the genuinely Higher momentum and half-life-ratio items that had leaked into a takeaway, an exam tip, practice types and flashcards. Also fixed: two invented exam claims, a reversed beta-penetration statement, a half-life key that gave 0.079 for 0.0804 and asked for units on a fraction, PAG terminology in a question type, and a PET-only account of internal imaging that never gave the spec's gamma-tracer method. Every other value, equation, nuclear equation, graph claim and answer key recomputed clean. Lesson 1 has no findings.
